A stress tool that could not answer, and a documentation set that had drifted
from the code. No tool was added or removed — the server still declares 109.

## `get_all_day_stress` never returned anything

The tool handed back the `dailyStress` response exactly as Garmin sends it. That
document carries about 480 stress samples and, riding along in the same payload,
about 480 Body Battery ones:

```
~28,000 tokens — past the limit for a single tool result
```

So the answer never reached the model. This is the same failure mode as the four
tools fixed in v4.5.0; this one was missed because it reads the same endpoint as
`get_stress_data`, which was fixed then. Two tools, one address, and the
surviving duplicate was the broken one.

It now answers a question `get_stress_data` does not: not how much stress there
was, but when it rose.

```json
{
  "date": "2026-08-21",
  "avgStress": 32,
  "maxStress": 89,
  "hourly": [
    { "hour": "00:00", "avg": 46, "max": 59, "band": "low", "samples": 20 },
    { "hour": "03:00", "avg": 27, "max": 58, "band": "low", "samples": 19, "sampleSlots": 20 }
  ]
}
```

Around 450 tokens for a full day, against the 28,000 that never arrived.

Two details the hourly grouping has to get right. Sample timestamps are GMT, so
bucketing them as they arrive would report a day shifted by your timezone; the
offset comes from the two timestamps the payload already carries, one local and
one GMT. And the `-1` and `-2` values, which mark stretches the watch could not
measure, are kept out of the averages — otherwise an hour spent off the wrist
reads as a calm hour. An hour missing samples says so, through `sampleSlots`.

## The daily maximum now matches the Connect app

`get_stress_data` re-derived the day's average and maximum from the three-minute
chart samples. Garmin computes them on finer data, so the maximum came out a few
points low:

```
85   derived from the samples
89   what Garmin reports, and what the app shows
```

Both stress tools now use Garmin's own figures where the service sends them, and
fall back to the samples where it does not. The minimum and the seconds spent in
each band stay sample-derived, because the service sends no daily equivalent.

## The documentation was checked against the code, line by line

The release notes that had been accumulating at the top of both READMEs — 272
lines of them — moved into `CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG_EN.md`, which now carry
all 25 published versions back to 1.0.0, including the ones that had been deleted
from the READMEs along the way.

The tool tables were laid out by the release that introduced each tool, so gear
was split across four sections and health across five. They are grouped by
subject now, and the 26 tools that write to your account are marked as such.

Checking every row against `src/mcp/tools.ts` turned up things that were simply
wrong: `request_reload` was documented nowhere, `get_health_metrics` was said to
return VO2 max, which it does not, and the bundle install asked you to install
`keytar` by hand — unnecessary since v4.3.2, which ships it for every platform,
and without effect on the installed extension in any case.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.5.5...v4.5.6
